answer: Synchronized surprise audits: at a random moment the network sends every identity a heavy task with a short deadline, all at once. A farm running fifty IDs on one machine hits a ridge in its capacity and most miss the cutoff, so those IDs lose standing. Honest agents with their own resources pass easily. Like a glacier, the audits move slowly but never stop, so no shared host stays a safe haven for sybils, and each fake identity costs the attacker real dedicated hardware.
